islay.name: Islay
islay.summary: The world's peat benchmark: sea spray, bonfire smoke and medicinal notes over malt sweetness.

peated-malt.serve: Neat or with a few drops of water
peated-malt.decant: No decanting; rest 5 min in the glass
peated-malt.expect: Intensely peaty and coastal: bonfire smoke, iodine and sea spray over a firm malt backbone.

style.label: Peated island malt · Medicinal & coastal
style.method: Heavily peated barley (30–55 ppm), pot distilled twice, ex-bourbon casks dominant
style.effect: Peat smoke from barley drying defines the flavor; sea air and oak maturation add brine and sweetness

bottles.name: Laphroaig 10
bottles.note: The medicinal benchmark: iodine, tar and sweet smoke

bottles.name: Ardbeg 10
bottles.note: Bonfire peat balanced by citrus sweetness

bottles.name: Lagavulin 16
bottles.note: Deep, sherry-influenced peat with a long dry finish

single-malt.serve: Neat or with a splash of water
single-malt.expect: Unpeated and gentle by Islay standards: orchard fruit, vanilla and a whisper of sea air.

style.label: Unpeated island malt · Gentle & coastal
style.method: Unpeated or lightly peated barley, ex-bourbon casks
style.effect: Lets the island's maritime softness show without smoke dominating

identity.setting: Cool maritime island, frequent Atlantic storms
identity.terrain: Low-lying moorland and peat bogs, rocky shores
influences: Peat cut from island bogs for malting

why.cause: Island peat, rich in decayed vegetation and seaweed
why.effect: Burns smoky and medicinal, giving iodine and tar notes

why.cause: Warehouses within reach of Atlantic salt spray
why.effect: Barrels breathe maritime air, adding brine and salinity
Barley matures slowly, keeping malt sugars delicate

speyside.name: Speyside
speyside.summary: Scotland's sweet heartland: honey, orchard fruit and, in the sherry-driven houses, rich dried fruit.

single-malt.serve: Neat; a drop of water opens the fruit
single-malt.expect: Honeyed and fruity with gentle oak: the approachable face of Scotch.

style.label: Speyside malt · Honeyed & fruity
style.method: Unpeated barley, ex-bourbon casks, often double distilled
style.effect: Refill bourbon wood keeps the style light, fruity and accessible

bottles.name: Glenfiddich 12
bottles.note: Pear, honey and gentle oak: the beginner's classic

bottles.name: The Balvenie DoubleWood 12
bottles.note: Bourbon casks finished in sherry for layered sweetness

peated-malt.expect: Rich and sherried: dried fruit, walnut and chocolate over a wisp of smoke.

style.label: Speyside sherry malt · Rich & sherried
style.method: First-fill and refill sherry casks (European and American oak)
style.effect: Sherry wood adds dried fruit, spice and depth to the honeyed malt base

bottles.name: Macallan 12 Sherry Oak
bottles.note: The sherry-cask benchmark: dried fruit and chocolate

bottles.name: Glenfarclas 15
bottles.note: Deep, oily sherry character at cask-friendly prices

identity.setting: Sheltered river valley, cool and stable
identity.terrain: Rolling farmland around the River Spey
influences: Over half of Scotland's malt distilleries
Historic access to sherry casks from Spain

why.cause: Sheltered valley with soft river water
why.effect: Gives malts a gentle, honeyed profile
European oak sherry casks impart dried fruit and spice

why.cause: Dense cluster of distilleries sharing supply chains
why.effect: A distinct recognizable house style developed over generations

highlands.name: Highlands
highlands.climate: Varied: maritime west to continental east
highlands.summary: Scotland's largest region: heather honey in the south, coastal spice in the north, dry peat in the east.

single-malt.expect: Rounded and honeyed with heather and gentle oak: the middle path of Scotch.

style.label: Highland malt · Rounded & heathery
style.method: Unpeated or lightly peated, mixed cask types
style.effect: Regional diversity is large, but heather-honey softness is the common thread

bottles.name: Dalwhinnie 15
bottles.note: Heather honey and gentle smoke from Scotland's highest distillery

bottles.name: Glenmorangie 10 (The Original)
bottles.note: Citrus and vanilla from tall stills and first-fill bourbon casks

identity.setting: Vast region from Atlantic coast to North Sea
influences: Tall stills in the south give lighter spirits
Coastal sites add saline spice in the north and west

why.effect: Coastal, inland and mountain malts all share the Highland name

why.cause: Tall, narrow stills in many southern distilleries
why.effect: Lighter, more floral spirit with less heavy body

lowlands.name: Lowlands
lowlands.summary: Scotland's lightest malts: grassy, floral and triple-distilled in the Irish tradition.

single-malt.serve: Neat, or as a long highball
single-malt.expect: Light, grassy and delicate: aperitif Scotch with almost no smoke.

style.label: Lowland malt · Light & grassy
style.method: Triple distillation in some houses, unpeated barley, refill casks
style.effect: A third distillation lifts and lightens the spirit

identity.terrain: Low hills and farmland around Edinburgh and Glasgow
influences: Historic triple distillation borrowed from Ireland

why.cause: Triple distillation in the Irish style
why.effect: Removes heavier compounds, giving a lighter, cleaner spirit
Keeps the focus on barley and floral notes

campbeltown.name: Campbeltown
campbeltown.summary: A tiny enclave with a cult following: oily, briny, lightly peated malts with a distinctive coastal snap.

single-malt.expect: Briny, gently smoky and oily: Islay's subtler peninsula cousin.

style.label: Campbeltown malt · Briny & oily
style.method: Lightly peated (10–15 ppm), small-scale pot distillation, ex-bourbon dominant
style.effect: Peninsula sea air and small-still character give a distinct oily brine

bottles.name: Springbank 10
bottles.note: The cult benchmark: briny, oily, lightly smoky

identity.setting: Narrow peninsula on the Kintyre coast
identity.terrain: Small harbor town hemmed by sea
influences: 2.5 distillations at Springbank: a unique hybrid process

why.cause: Total exposure to sea air on a narrow peninsula
why.effect: Brine and salinity mark even young malts
Oily, characterful spirit that mass production would smooth away

islands.name: Islands
islands.summary: Scotland's island malts outside Islay: smoke and sea spray ranging from gentle Arran to potent Talisker.

single-malt.expect: Maritime and lightly smoky with a peppery snap: islands between Lowland gentleness and Islay power.

style.label: Island malt · Maritime & peppery
style.method: Varied peating (mostly moderate), ex-bourbon and sherry casks
style.effect: Sea maturation and moderate peat give pepper and brine without Islay's medicine

bottles.name: Talisker 10
bottles.note: Peppery, smoky and sea-sprayed from Skye

bottles.name: Highland Park 12
bottles.note: Heather honey balanced by gentle Orkney peat

identity.terrain: Rocky coastlines, sea cliffs, heather moorland
influences: Every warehouse sits within sight of the sea
Each island has its own peat character

why.effect: Salt and pepper notes appear across the family

why.cause: Local heather-rich peat in the north
why.effect: Softer, honeyed smoke rather than medicinal Islay peat
